Rashi on Sukkah 11b:10:1.english: We do not derive lulav from sukkah - To disqualify in it that which is [already] made.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:11:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - אם הוה סבירא להו לתרוייהו לולב צריך אגד ושייכא ביה עשיה, דכולי עלמא דילפינן לולב מסוכה למיפסל, ולקיטתן לאו זו היא עשייתן:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:11:1.english: And if you wish, say - If both of them held that a *lulav* requires binding and [therefore] "making" applies to it, everyone [would agree] that we derive *lulav* from *sukkah* to disqualify [it], and [that] picking them is not their making.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:11:2.hebrew: ר"ש סבר לולב צריך אגד - לאגוד שלשה המינים, ושייכא ביה עשיה, ועל כרחך מבעוד יום אגדו עם ענביו, וכי לוקטו בי"ט, הוה ליה מן העשוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:11:2.english: Rabbi Shimon holds that a lulav requires binding - To bind the three species [together], and [thus] an act of making applies to it; and perforce, while it was still day [before the Festival], he bound it with its berries, and when he picked them on the Festival, it is [disqualified as] "from that which has already been made."

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:12:1.hebrew: לא ילפינן - לא למדוה, ואין אדם דן גזירה שוה מעצמו, אלא א"כ למדו מרבו, ורבו מרבו, עד משה רבינו. ושמא מקראות הללו לא לדרוש גזירה שוה נכתבו:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:12:1.english: We do not derive - They did not learn it [by tradition]; and a person does not derive a gezeirah shavah [verbal analogy] on his own, unless he learned it from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher, [all the way] to Moses our teacher. And perhaps these verses were not written to expound a gezeirah shavah.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:13:1.hebrew: ואנוהו התנאה לפניו במצות - סוכה נאה, לולב נאה, ציצית נאה:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:13:1.english: “And I will glorify Him” — beautify yourself before Him with mitzvot - A beautiful sukkah, a beautiful lulav, [and] beautiful tzitzit.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:14:1.hebrew: ואד יעלה מן הארץ - שמע מינה עננים גידולי קרקע נינהו, וסוכה מעננים ילפינן, שהרי זכר לענני כבוד הוא, כדכתיב: כי בסוכות הושבתי, ומתרגמינן: ארי במטלות ענניי:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:14:1.english: And there went up a mist from the earth - Learn from this that clouds are products of the ground, and we derive [the laws of] a sukkah from clouds, for it is a commemoration of the clouds of glory, as it is written: "For I made [the children of Israel] dwell in booths," and we translate [in the Targum]: "For in the shelter of clouds."

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:14:2.hebrew: אין מקבל טומאה - דלא נאמרה טומאה אלא בכלים, ואוכלין, ומשקין, ואדם, וזה איננו אחד מאלה:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:14:2.english: Is not susceptible to ritual impurity - For ritual impurity was stated only regarding utensils, food, liquids, and human beings, and this [mist] is not one of these.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:15:1.english: They were clouds of glory - [The] booths about which Scripture states that He made them reside in the wilderness.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:15:2.english: Actual booths - Because of the sun, at the time of their encampment, they would make booths.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:15:3.english: What can be said - Who is to say to us that they were not covered with utensils, garments, and hides?

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:16:1.hebrew: כי חגיגה - כל בהמה לרבי יוחנן גדולי קרקע הן, שמן הקרקע גדילים וניזונין. אבל דגים ומלח וכמהין ופטריות לאו גידולי קרקע נינהו. וגבי מעשר קרינן להו לבהמות גידולי קרקע, דאמר קרא (דברים י״ד:כ״ו) ונתתה הכסף בכל אשר תאוה נפשך וגו', מה הפרט מפורש פרי מפרי וגידולי קרקע וכו'. ומיהו, כיון דלא קמה מילתייהו דרבי יוחנן, דהא פרכינן עלה: אי מה חגיגה בעלי חיים וכו', וילפינן טעמא מגרנך ומיקבך, לא סמכינן עלה לאכשורי לסכך בעורות. דנהי דגידולי הארץ איקרי על שם שהארץ מגדלתן במרעה ופרנסה, אבל גידולים מן הארץ לא אקרי אלא דבר הצומח מן הקרקע, ולא בהמות; דתניא בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ ד' פט.): פועלים אוכלין בדבר שגידולו מן הארץ, וגמר מלא תחסום שור בדישו: מה דיש מיוחד דבר שגידולו מן הארץ כו', יצא החולב והמחבץ והמגבן, אלמא לאו גידולין מן הארץ קרי להו תנא:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:16:1.english: Like the Festival peace-offering - According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, all animals are produce of the ground, since they grow and are nourished from the ground. However, fish, salt, truffles, and mushrooms are not produce of the ground. And regarding [second] tithe, we call animals produce of the ground, as the verse states (Deuteronomy 14:26): "And you shall spend the money for whatever your soul desires, etc."; just as the specific item is explicitly an offspring from offspring and produce of the ground, etc. However, since Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement did not stand—for we challenge it: "If [it is likened to] a Festival peace-offering, [perhaps just as a Festival peace-offering is] a living animal, etc.?" and we derive the reason from "from your threshing floor and from your wine vat"—we do not rely on it to validate roofing [a sukka] with hides. For although they are called "produce of the earth" because the earth raises them through pasture and sustenance, "growth from the earth" applies only to something that grows from the ground, and not to animals. As it is taught in [the chapter] HaSokher Et HaPo'alim (Bava Metzia 89a): "Laborers may eat [from that which they work with only] in the case of something whose growth is from the earth"; and it is derived from "You shall not muzzle an ox in its threshing": Just as threshing is characterized by [being performed on] something whose growth is from the earth, etc., this excludes one who milks [an animal], one who churns [butter], and one who makes cheese. Evidently, the Tanna does not call them "growth from the earth."

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:1:1.hebrew: בעינן כנף בשעת פתיל - בשעה שפותלו, שתולה בו הפתילים, בעינן כנף אחד ולא שנים:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:1:1.english: We require a corner at the time of the strand - At the time that he threads it, that is, when he hangs the strands in it, we require one corner and not two.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:2:1.hebrew: לעולם - ואפילו מפסקן לשנים לאחר קישור, וקשיא לרב:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:2:1.english: Actually - And even if he cuts them into two after tying, and it is a difficulty for Rav.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:4:1.english: And [if] he placed roofing atop them, it is unfit - And we do not read in the baraita: "If the roofing was greater than them, or if he cut them."

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:6:1.hebrew: דשלפינהו שלופי - פשחן מן האילן עד שניתקן, ומתוך שאין קציצתן ניכרת כל כך, ששוכבין ראשי פשיחתן אצל האילן, לא הוי עשיה מעלייא:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:6:1.english: Where he pulled them off - He tore them from the tree until he detached them, and since their cutting is not so noticeable, as the ends where they were torn off lie next to the tree, it is not a proper [act of] preparation.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:6:2.english: In any case, "If one attached them and afterward cut [them]" is a difficulty for Rav - For he deems [them] fit.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:7:1.english: [Parallel to a dispute between] Tannaim - Whether we say that their cutting is their preparation, or not.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:7:2.hebrew: עבר וליקטן - ענבי ההדס, דתנן לקמן (סוכה ד' לב:): אם היו ענביו מרובין מעליו, פסול, דהוה ליה מנומר ולא הדר הוא. ואם מיעטו, כשר, ואין ממעטין בי"ט, דמתקן מנא להכשיר את הפסול. וקתני בברייתא: עבר על דברי חכמים שאמרו אין ממעטין בי"ט, ולקטן בי"ט, פסול:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:7:2.english: [If] he transgressed and picked them - [This refers to the] berries of the myrtle branch, as we learned below (Sukkah 32b): If its berries were more numerous than its leaves, it is unfit, for it is speckled and is not beautiful; and if he diminished them, it is fit. But one may not diminish [them] on the Festival, because he is repairing a utensil by rendering fit that which was unfit. And it is taught in the baraita: [If] he transgressed the words of the Sages who said that one may not diminish [them] on the Festival, and picked them on the Festival, [it is] unfit.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:8:1.english: They assumed - The Rabbis of the study hall, who wished to deduce from it that they disagree over [whether] their picking is the completion of their preparation.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:8:2.english: That everyone - Both of these Tanna'im hold [this].

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:8:3.hebrew: לולב צריך אגד - לאגוד שלשה המינין כאחד, ושייכא בה עשיה:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:8:3.english: A lulav requires binding - To bind the three species together, and [thus] an act of making applies to it.

Rashi on Sukkah 11b:8:4.hebrew: וילפינן לולב מסוכה - בבנין אב: מה מצינו בסוכה, שיש בה מעשה והקפידה תורה על העשוי בפסול, אף לולב כן:
Rashi on Sukkah 11b:8:4.english: And we derive lulav from sukkah - Through a binyan av [paradigm]: Just as we find with regard to a sukkah, that it involves an act [of making] and the Torah was strict regarding that which is made in invalidity, so too, lulav is the same.

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:10:1.hebrew: והכא במילף לולב מסוכה קמיפלגי - והא דאיפלגו בעבר וליקטן, ולא איפלגו בליקטן מערב י"ט — דבעי לאשמועינן: אין דיחוי אצל מצות, כדאיתא בפרק לולב הגזול (לקמן סוכה דף לג.). א"נ, משום דמעי"ט היה יכול לתקן לכתחילה: להתיר אוגדו ולחזור ולאוגדו. אי נמי, כדפי' בקונטרס לקמן, דנקט פלוגתייהו בי"ט למימר דבתר אוגדיה פליגי, דהא בי"ט לא אגיד ליה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:10:1.english: And here, they disagree regarding deriving lulav from sukka - And as for the fact that they disputed [a case where] he transgressed and picked them [on the Festival], and did not dispute [a case where] he picked them on the eve of the Festival — [this is] because [the Tanna] wanted to teach us that there is no [permanent] disqualification [deḥui] regarding mitzvot, as is stated in chapter Lulav HaGazul (below, Sukkah 33a). Alternatively, [it is] because on the eve of the Festival he would have been able to rectify [it] ab initio: to untie its binding and bind it again. Alternatively, as explained by Rashi [the Kuntres] below, [the Tanna] formulated their dispute on the Festival to indicate that they disagree [where he picked them] after its binding, for on the Festival he would not bind it.

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:12:1.hebrew: לקיחה לקיחה לא ילפינן - בריש קדושין (דף ב.) ילפי' קיחה קיחה משדה עפרון, אבל הכא לא ילפינן גזירה שוה דלקיחה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:12:1.english: We do not derive "taking" [from] "taking" - At the beginning of Kiddushin (2a), we derive "taking" [from] "taking" from the field of Ephron, but here we do not derive a verbal analogy of "taking".

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:16:1.hebrew: מקיש סוכה לחגיגה - הכא מייתי קרא דחג הסוכות תעשה לך, ולעיל (סוכה דף ט.), דאסרינן עצי סוכה משום דאיתקש לחגיגה, מייתי קרא דחג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה':
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:16:1.english: It likens sukkah to the Festival peace-offering - Here, [the Gemara] cites the verse: "You shall make the festival of Sukkot for yourself"; whereas above (Sukkah 9a), where we prohibit the wood of the sukkah because it was equated to the Festival peace-offering, it cites the verse: "The festival of Sukkot is seven days to the Lord."

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:16:2.hebrew: וגידולו מן הארץ - בריש בכל מערבין (עירובין דף כז:) גבי מעשר שני, דכתיב ונתתה הכסף בבקר ובצאן, חשיב בהמה גידולו מן הארץ. אבל בפ' השוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פט.) גבי דיש, ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף יז.) גבי הענקה, לא חשיב בהמה גידולי קרקע; דלגבי דבר היוצא מן הקרקע ממש, כגון דיש וגידולין, לאו יוצא מן הקרקע היא, אלא שהיא גדילה מן הקרקע:
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:16:2.english: And its growth is from the ground - At the beginning of Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 27b), regarding the second tithe, where it is written: "And you shall spend the money on cattle and on sheep" (Deuteronomy 14:26), [the Gemara] considers an animal to be [something whose] growth is from the ground. However, in the chapter HaSokher et HaPo'alim (Bava Metzia 89a), regarding threshing, and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (17a), regarding the severance gift [ha'anaka], it does not consider an animal to be produce of the ground; for in comparison to something that literally emerges from the ground, such as [the produce of] threshing and crops, it does not emerge from the ground, but rather it grows [is nourished] from the ground.

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:2:1.hebrew: פסולין לעולם - כולהו אמוראי וכולה שיטתא כשמואל, ולא אמר קציצתן זו עשייתן, וגבי סוכה צריך נענוע:
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:2:1.english: They are unfit forever - All the Amoraim and the entire progression of the Gemara follow Shmuel, and [he] does not say: "Their cutting is their preparation," and regarding a sukkah, [one] needs to move [the roofing].

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:6:1.hebrew: דשלפינהו שלופי - קצת קשה, דהא מפרש טעמא בברייתא משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי. וי"ל: אסמכתא בעלמא הוא. אי נמי, הכא מיירי כשנפשח ומעורה בקליפה ואין יכול להחיות לה, כי ההיא דפ' העור והרוטב (חולין דף קכז:), דאע"ג דחשיב כתלוש, מ"מ כיון דלא נקצץ לגמרי לא אמרינן זו היא עשיה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:6:1.english: Where he pulled them off - This is somewhat difficult, for the reason is explicitly stated in the *baraita* as being due to [the principle]: "Prepare [it]," and not from that which has already been prepared. And one can say: It is a mere *asmakhta* [supportive allusion]. Alternatively, here [the *baraita*] is dealing with [a case] where [the vine] was torn [from the tree] and remains attached [only] by the bark, and cannot sustain itself, like that [case] in the chapter [entitled] *HaOhr VeHaRotev* (Chullin 127b), where even though it is considered detached, nevertheless, since it was not cut completely, we do not say: "This is its making" [to render it fit roofing].

Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:7:1.hebrew: דברי ר"ש בן יהוצדק - תנא היה. ואפשר שזה הוא הנזכר בכמה מקומות בש"ס: א"ר יוחנן משום ר"ש בן יהוצדק. ואין זה הוא דפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כו.), דקרנהו ריש לקיש רועי בקר, ואמר להו ר' יוחנן: אי קרינכו רועי צאן, מאי עבידנא לכו; דלא הוה מהדר ליה הכי, אלא מוחה היה על כבוד רבו:
Tosafot on Sukkah 11b:7:1.english: The statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak - He was a Tanna. And it is possible that he is the one mentioned in several places in the Talmud: "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak." And this is not the one of chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26a), where Reish Lakish called them "cattle herders," and Rabbi Yochanan said to them: "If he had called you shepherds, what could I have done for you?" — for [Rabbi Yochanan] would not have replied to him in this manner; rather, he would have protested for the honor of his teacher.
